warning: These are adapter implementation baselines, not live availability guarantees. Offline contract tests do not prove a model/account supports a capability. Every adapter must emit a model- and configuration-specific capability snapshot at runtime.

semantic_notes: Tool calls are returned as structured output items and client tools remain application-executed.
Canonical tool_choice maps to native required/specific controls and returned arguments are locally schema-validated before execution.
Structured outputs still require local schema and business-rule validation.
Response and conversation identifiers must not become canonical project state.
The adapter sends store=false and still requires live model/account conformance before enabling capabilities.
Client tool_use and provider server tools have different execution ownership.
Canonical required/specific tool choice maps to any/tool; model and thinking compatibility still require live conformance.
pause_turn and model_context_window_exceeded must remain distinct from normal completion.
Structured output support varies by model and hosting surface.
The client-tool adapter does not claim provider-hosted server tools and still requires live conformance.
Function calls are suggestions; the application executes functions and returns results.
Canonical required/specific tool choice maps to ANY with an optional allowedFunctionNames restriction.
Compositional and parallel tool behavior must be normalized without assuming one call per turn.
Transient 429 and 503 responses require bounded backoff, not silent provider switching.
Function-call IDs may require a visible synthetic identifier when the API omits one; live conformance remains pending.
The adapter targets the standard API at /api/paas/v4/chat/completions and must not be pointed at a Coding Plan endpoint.
GLM-5.3 standard Model API availability is still marked as forthcoming by the official model page; an API key alone is not availability evidence.
Structured output is prompt-enforced with a bounded schema instruction, uses provider json_object mode, and is locally validated; it is not provider-native strict JSON Schema.
Canonical Task, Assignment, and execution-contract metadata remains local and is not transmitted in the provider payload.
The adapter requires an exact returned model match and never accepts automatic routing from another requested model as fallback.
Client function tools use tool_choice=auto only and permit at most one function call per turn; parallel and provider-hosted tools are rejected.

GLM thinking remains enabled with an explicit low, high, or max reasoning effort; tool-turn reasoning_content is retained only in bounded adapter-private memory for exact handback and is never normalized into ModelResponse or project records.
Each Attempt requires a fresh single-active adapter instance and an explicit final discard of its ephemeral continuation state.
Provider-reported monetary cost is unavailable; the execution budget must fail closed rather than infer a tariff.
Actual capabilities and data policy depend on the selected downstream provider and model.
Routing and fallback must be logged and constrained by require_parameters, region, retention, and collection policy.
Gateway compatibility does not erase downstream provider semantics.
